newsitem.title: USA: Weekly jobless claims down in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Weekly jobless claims down in latest week.

text.p: The number of Americans signing up for first-time state unemployment benefits fell unexpectedly last week by 22,000, the Labour Department said Thursday.
New filings fell to 319,000 in the week ended Oct. 5, compared with a revised 341,000 a week earlier. Wall Street economists had expected claims in the latest week to inch up to 342,000.
The inflation-sensitive U.S. Treasury bond market slipped after release of the report and analysts said an already jittery stock market was likely to follow it lower.
The department's four-week moving average of jobless claims -- considered a more accurate gauge of employment trends -- fell to 332,250 from the previous week's revised average of 334,750.

The department said four states and one territory reported decreases in initial claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended Sept. 28, the latest period for which that data were available.
They were North Carolina, with 4,591 fewer filings; Georgia, with 1,550; Florida, with 1,205; and South Carolina, with 1,098. Puerto Rico had 3,574 fewer claims.
North Carolina attributed the falloff in claims to fewer layoffs in the construction and textile industries.
Georgia linked the decrease to fewer layoffs in the textile and food industries, while South Carolina cited fewer layoffs in the food industry.
Florida reported fewer layoffs in the construction, trade and service industries, as well as in manufacturing and agriculture. Puerto Rico had no comment.
Tennessee, with 1,381 additional claims, was the only state reporting an increase in claims exceeding 1,000 in the week.
It said increased claims activity was due to layoffs in the food, apparel, furniture, paper, fabricated metals, industrial machinery and electronic equipment industries.
